title: iPhone in Vietnam: where to buy and what it costs (2026)
description: Apple Vietnam's November 2026 iPhone prices, the authorised shops, what VN/A means for warranty, instalments, returns and the VAT refund when you leave.
h1: Buying an iPhone in Vietnam: where to buy, what it costs and what to check
intro: You can buy an iPhone in Vietnam from Apple's own online store for Vietnam, open since May 2023, or from authorised resellers such as TopZone, FPT Shop, CellphoneS and Viettel Store. Vietnam-market phones carry the code VN/A. Apple's list prices in Vietnam include all taxes and delivery is free. Apple's warranty lasts one year, and Apple may limit warranty repairs to the country where the phone was first sold.
keyPoints: As of November 2026, Apple Vietnam's iPhone prices run from {{vnd:21999000}} for the iPhone 17e up to {{vnd:103999000}} for the 2TB iPhone Duo. Prices include tax and delivery is free.
Vietnam-market iPhones carry **VN/A** at the end of the part number. On the phone, go to Settings > General > About and look at the Model Number line.
Apple's one-year warranty lets Apple limit iPhone repairs to the country where the phone was first sold. Keep the VAT invoice, because authorised service centres ask for it.
Apple Vietnam's returns page says iPhones bought there generally can't be returned or exchanged unless they are faulty. Any refund goes only to a Vietnamese bank account in the payer's name.

When you leave the country you can claim back 85% of the VAT on an unused phone in its original packaging. The purchase must be at least {{vnd:2000000}} from one store on one day, and the VAT invoice cum tax refund declaration must be issued no more than 60 days before the date of departure.

sections.title: Where can you buy an iPhone in Vietnam?

blocks.text: The safest places to buy an iPhone in Vietnam are Apple's online store for Vietnam and Apple's authorised resellers. Both sell Vietnam-market phones that come with Apple's one-year warranty. Independent shops and secondhand sellers can be cheaper or quicker, but the checks are up to you.

Apple runs the **Apple Store online for Vietnam** (apple.com/vn) itself. Apple launched it from Ho Chi Minh City in May 2023, with instalments, trade-in and support in Vietnamese, according to [Apple's announcement](https://apple.com/newsroom/2023/05/apple-launches-apple-store-online-in-vietnam). If you would rather see the phone first, go to a reseller. Thế Giới Di Động's buyer's guide names TopZone (run with Thế Giới Di Động), FPT Shop, CellphoneS and Viettel Store as authorised Apple resellers.

blocks.text: Shortages around a new launch push people towards unofficial sellers. Vietnamnet reported on 16 September 2026 that smaller Ho Chi Minh City shops were charging up to about US$230 more than authorised retailers for the iPhone 18 Pro. It also reported that some retailers asked for extras costing nearly US$305 for launch-day delivery. VnExpress reported on 7 October 2026 that iPhone 18 Pro supplies stabilised quickly after the first sales period.

sections.title: How much does an iPhone cost in Vietnam?

blocks.text: According to Apple Vietnam's store pages, as of November 2026, a new iPhone costs from {{vnd:21999000}} (iPhone 17e) to {{vnd:103999000}} (iPhone Duo, 2TB). These prices include all taxes, and delivery is free on every order.

blocks.caption: Apple Vietnam iPhone prices by storage, from apple.com/vn, checked 22 November 2026

blocks.text: Older models now cost more than they did at launch. On 22 November 2026, Apple Vietnam's store showed the 256GB iPhone 17 at {{vnd:28999000}}. VnExpress reported that Apple raised the iPhone 17 by {{vnd:4000000}} on 10 September 2026, when the iPhone 18 Pro launched. According to the same report, Apple also raised the prices of the iPhone 17e, iPhone Air and iPhone 16 that day.

Resellers set their own prices, which often sit a little below Apple's. VnExpress reported on 7 October 2026 that some retailers had cut the iPhone 18 Pro by {{vnd:500000}}, to about {{vnd:38500000}} for 256GB. VnExpress added that the cut came from retailers, not Apple. To compare these prices with what you would pay at home, see [is it cheaper to buy an iPhone in Vietnam?](/guides/is-it-cheaper-to-buy-iphone-in-vietnam)

sections.title: Vietnam iPhone or imported: what VN/A means for the warranty

blocks.text: A Vietnam-market iPhone carries the region code **VN/A** at the end of its part number. Thế Giới Di Động's guide says a VN/A phone gets official repairs at Apple's authorised service centres across Vietnam. An imported phone (xách tay) may not.

The reason is in [Apple's one-year limited warranty](https://www.apple.com/legal/warranty/products/ios-warranty-row-english.html). Apple says it may restrict warranty service for iPhone to the country where Apple or its authorised distributors first sold the device. The same warranty says that if you need repairs outside that country, you may pay shipping and handling, and you must comply with customs rules. For a VN/A phone, Vietnam is the country of sale. Bear this in mind if you plan to take the phone home within its first year.

items.title: Open Settings
items.text: Go to Settings > General > About, as [Apple's support page](https://support.apple.com/en-us/106343) describes.

items.title: Read the part number
items.text: The part number sits to the right of the Model Number line. A Vietnam-market phone ends in VN/A. If you tap the part number, the screen shows the model number, which starts with A.

items.title: Check the box matches
items.text: In a shop, compare the serial number and IMEI on the box with what the phone shows under About. Ask for a VAT invoice before you leave.

blocks.title: Don't let anyone open the phone
blocks.text: Viet Nam News reported in May 2023 that Apple Vietnam refused some warranty claims because the phone had been opened. In one case the owner said she had never taken it to a repair shop. Use only authorised service centres while the phone is under warranty, and keep the invoice. If a claim is refused, the same report says you can complain through Apple's call centre and ask for a recheck.

sections.title: How to buy from Apple's online store in Vietnam

blocks.text: You choose a model on apple.com/vn, pay in full or in instalments, and Apple delivers the phone. It pays to know the payment and returns rules before you order, because they suit someone with a Vietnamese bank account.

items.title: Pick the phone
items.text: Choose a model, colour and storage on apple.com/vn. If you have an old device to trade in, add it here. Apple Trade In is run through a partner, and the partner can lower or refuse the quote after inspecting the device.

items.title: Choose how to pay
items.text: To pay in instalments with **MoMo**, you need a MoMo e-wallet account and approval from MoMo's credit partners. The order must be at least {{vnd:3750000}} and you pay 20% upfront. Credit card instalments over 3, 6, 9 or 12 months work with cards from ACB, BIDV, HSBC, Shinhan, Techcombank, VIB, Vietcombank and VPBank. Each order must be at least {{vnd:3000000}}, debit cards don't qualify, and fees depend on the bank and term.

items.title: Check before it ships
items.text: If you cancel after Apple starts preparing the order, there is a 20% restocking fee.

items.title: Watch the price for 14 days
items.text: If Apple lowers the price within 14 days of delivery, you can ask for the difference back. Limited-time promotions don't count.

blocks.title: Returns are narrow
blocks.text: As of November 2026, [Apple Vietnam's returns page](https://www.apple.com/vn/shop/help/returns_refund) says products bought from Apple Store in Vietnam generally can't be returned or exchanged, except faulty ones. It also says refunds go only to a Vietnamese bank account in the payer's name and can't be sent abroad. Before returning a device, turn off Find My. If you don't yet bank locally, see [banking and sending money home from Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/banking-and-sending-money-home-from-vietnam).

sections.title: Buying an iPhone near you: what to check in the shop

blocks.text: In Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi and other large cities, the authorised chains have many branches. The nearest one is usually easiest to find through the chain's own store finder or [Apple's location finder for Vietnam](https://locate.apple.com/vn/en/). In any shop, check these things before you pay:

items: **VN/A** at the end of the part number, unless you have decided to buy an imported phone and accept the warranty risk.
A **VAT invoice** in your name or the buyer's name. Apple's authorised service centres ask for it, and you need it for a VAT refund.
Any **bundles** you don't want. At launch, some retailers made extra warranty packages or accessories a condition of early delivery.
For a used phone, **Find My turned off** and signed out of the seller's Apple Account while you watch. Also check the coverage status against the serial number.

blocks.text: Check the SIM before you choose a model. According to Apple Vietnam's page, the iPhone Air works only with eSIM and has no physical SIM tray. To use it, you need a carrier that supports eSIM. Our [SIM and eSIM guide](/esim-vietnam-guide) explains how to get a local number. If you only need a basic phone for a local SIM, see [the cheapest phones in Vietnam](/guides/cheapest-phone-in-vietnam).

sections.title: Can you get the VAT back on an iPhone when you leave Vietnam?

blocks.text: Yes, if the phone is unused and you take it out of the country. Foreigners and overseas Vietnamese with a valid foreign passport can claim back 85% of the VAT paid when they leave through a border gate that offers refunds. This is under Decree 181/2025/ND-CP and Circular 84/2026/TT-BTC, as [LuatVietnam summarises the rules](https://english.luatvietnam.vn/legal-news/conditions-for-vat-refunds-for-foreigners-upon-departure-4729-110896-article.html). The bank acting as refund agent keeps the other 15%.

blocks.caption: VAT refund conditions under Decree 181/2025/ND-CP and Circular 84/2026/TT-BTC, as summarised by LuatVietnam and read on 22 November 2026

blocks.title: Only for a phone you haven't used
blocks.text: Because the phone must be unused, the refund suits a phone bought as a gift or bought just before you leave. It doesn't suit a phone you have been using here. If you are leaving for good, [selling up before you leave Vietnam](/selling-up-before-you-leave-vietnam) explains how to sell your current phone along with everything else.

faqs.q: Where can I buy an iPhone in Vietnam?
faqs.a: You can buy an iPhone in Vietnam from Apple's own online store for Vietnam (apple.com/vn), which Apple launched in May 2023. You can also buy from authorised resellers such as TopZone, FPT Shop, CellphoneS and Viettel Store. Both sell Vietnam-market iPhones coded VN/A, which come with Apple's one-year warranty. Independent shops and secondhand sellers also sell iPhones, but you have to check the region code, the invoice and the warranty status yourself.

faqs.q: How much is an iPhone in Vietnam?
faqs.a: According to Apple Vietnam's store, as of November 2026, the iPhone 17e is the cheapest new iPhone and the 2TB iPhone Duo is the most expensive. The iPhone 17, iPhone Air, iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max sit in between. Apple's Vietnam prices include all taxes and delivery is free. Authorised resellers often sell slightly below Apple's price. The full price table, model by model, is on this page.

faqs.q: What does VN/A mean on an iPhone?
faqs.a: VN/A is the region code at the end of an iPhone's part number. It marks a phone made for the Vietnamese market. A VN/A iPhone gets official repairs at Apple's authorised service centres in Vietnam. To find the code, open Settings, then General, then About, and read the part number next to Model Number. Imported iPhones carry other region codes.

faqs.q: Does the Apple warranty work on an iPhone bought in Vietnam?
faqs.a: An iPhone bought in Vietnam comes with Apple's one-year limited warranty, which starts on the original purchase date. Apple's warranty terms say Apple may restrict iPhone warranty service to the country where the phone was first sold. A VN/A iPhone is therefore safest to repair in Vietnam. Outside Vietnam, you may have to pay shipping and handling and deal with customs rules. Keep the VAT invoice, because authorised centres ask for it.

faqs.q: Can foreigners get a tax refund on an iPhone in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Foreigners with a valid foreign passport can claim back 85% of the VAT on an iPhone when they leave Vietnam, under Circular 84/2026/TT-BTC. The phone must be unused and in its original packaging, bought from a store authorised for VAT refunds, and taken out of the country. The VAT invoice cum tax refund declaration must be issued no more than 60 days before the date of departure. A minimum spend applies per store per day.

faqs.q: Can I pay for an iPhone in instalments in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Apple's online store for Vietnam offers iPhone instalments in two ways. The first is through MoMo, which needs a MoMo e-wallet account, approval from MoMo's credit partners and a 20% down payment. The second is with a credit card from a listed Vietnamese bank over 3, 6, 9 or 12 months. Debit cards don't qualify for Apple Vietnam's instalments, and fees depend on the bank and the term.

faqs.q: Can I return an iPhone bought from Apple in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Apple Vietnam's returns page says products bought from Apple Store in Vietnam generally can't be returned or exchanged, except faulty ones, which you report to Apple's customer care. Cancelling an order after Apple starts preparing it costs a 20% restocking fee. Refunds go only to a Vietnamese bank account in the payer's name. If Apple lowers the price within 14 days of delivery, you can claim the difference.
